records.region: Northeastern Alaska, unnamed western headward approach through Kongakut River to Siku Lagoon.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity; not a uniform name for every selected reach
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route has a supported representative Kongakut River identity. An unnamed western headwater approach connects to the named river; the complete selected mountain and coastal corridor continues through the Kongakut delta to Siku Lagoon. The headward name remains null, and no whole-feature scalar name or product change is applied.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary-scale geographic correspondence of the one retained rendered fragment and all 42 internal line parts. Overlapping original cartography covers the chosen unnamed opening, its full tributary connection, the named receiving trunk, material tributary confluences, lower distributary split and actual lagoon receiving setting. Private orientation aids were used only to follow the pinned selection; original pixels were read separately. No substantial unmapped connector remains. This is not precision geometry validation or formal name-boundary verification.
records.supported_name_scope: The named Kongakut receiving trunk, mountain-valley corridor and selected delta branch support a representative system identity. The western selected headward feeder and approach retain null names. Siku Lagoon is the receiving waterbody, not a river-name alias.

component_scope_limits: The named Kongakut receiving trunk, mountain-valley corridor and selected delta branch support a representative system identity. The western selected headward feeder and approach retain null names. Siku Lagoon is the receiving waterbody, not a river-name alias.
The initial feeder and selected western approach have no established name in this finding; a nearby named trunk is not used to name them.
Generalized model segments are locally offset from or clip mapped bends; no bank-level, vertex-level, source-point or shoreline precision is asserted.
The map supports the selected corridor and delta connection, not present discharge, seasonality, perennial flow, current delta channels or tidal state.
The composite map refresh date does not establish the survey date of every feature.
Formal registry status, naming date, aliases, Indigenous-name equivalence and Korean forms remain unverified.

records.region: Seward Peninsula, western Alaska, Taylor–Kougarok–Kuzitrin drainage and connected Imuruk Basin–Tuksuk Channel–Grantley Harbor waters.
records.candidate_name_role: Kuzitrin River is the directly mapped lower receiving-river identity and the bounded representative identity of this selected drainage corridor. The selection approaches through an unnamed headward feeder, Taylor Creek and Kougarok River, then continues through the separate Imuruk Basin waterbody and Tuksuk Channel into Grantley Harbor. These components retain their individual identities; Kuzitrin is not assigned as a uniform name to the entire selection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route connects an unnamed feeder, Taylor Creek, Kougarok River and lower Kuzitrin River, then passes through Imuruk Basin and Tuksuk Channel into Grantley Harbor. Kuzitrin River is supported only as the representative receiving-river system identity; each named river and coastal-water component remains distinct.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic correspondence of the one selected mainstem fragment, including all 50 stored line subparts, against six readable original USGSTopo views. The chosen short opening, upper Taylor Creek turn, Taylor–Kougarok joining setting, Kougarok middle course and tributary junctions, Kougarok–Kuzitrin junction, lower braided Kuzitrin corridor, Imuruk Basin passage, Tuksuk Channel and actual Grantley Harbor terminal are covered. The generalized selection cuts local bends and is offset from mapped banks; no exact vertex correspondence, official natural source or precisely surveyed mouth is claimed. No substantial unviewed or unestablished through-connection remains at ordinary corridor scale.

These components retain their individual identities; Kuzitrin is not assigned as a uniform name to the entire selection.

records.region: Northern Ontario, Canada; Kinushseo River lowland corridor east of the Sutton drainage, toward the Hudson Bay coastal setting near Little Cape.
records.candidate_name_role: Directly supported middle and lower river component; provisional representative-system candidate only.
records.material_pending_reason: The original thematic maps establish the selected corridor only from their southern coverage boundary through the middle and lower river to the selected estuarine transition. The entire southern opening, long eastward headward course, possible waterbody passages and northward connection into that mapped corridor remain unestablished. The independent field-study location map does not resolve those links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Readable original OGS P.3651 and P.3641 maps show the continuous middle/lower Kinushseo corridor, its successive northward and eastward bends, side-stream junctions, and the widened estuarine approach. Sutton River lies separately to the west. The selected endpoint is at the eastern head of the wider Kinushseo estuarine reach; the mapped river continues northwest beyond the selection toward the coastal bay beside Little Cape and Hudson Bay. The model’s sea classification does not establish that its endpoint is already in open Hudson Bay. No claim is made that a nearby study lake or a named basin establishes the missing southern through-route.

records.region: Northeastern Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; Cañuelas–San Vicente–Brandsen approach and Samborombón corridor to Bahía Samborombón.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported middle/lower receiving-system candidate. The extreme western selected opening is unresolved, and the selected northern upper arm has a distinct Samborombón Chico identity.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable regional geography and a supported receiving name do not establish the entire selected western hydrological connection. The result is one source-material-pending case, not a completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Samborombón is supported for the mapped middle/lower receiving corridor and its mouth into Bahía Samborombón. The northern upper component near Brandsen is distinguished as Samborombón Chico. The complete western headward link is not established, so the single primary status is source-material pending. No accepted, scalar or Korean name is assigned, and no product change is authorized.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
